title: Understanding breakout-prone skin
content: Acne-prone skin benefits from a steady routine: gentle low-foam cleanser, lightweight non-comedogenic moisturizer, and daily SPF. Salicylic acid can help with congestion when used two to three nights per week. Avoid stacking multiple strong actives on the same night. Introduce one new product at a time and patch test first.

title: Breakout habits to avoid
content: Frequent face touching, harsh scrubs, over-washing, and changing products too often can worsen breakout patterns. Keep pillowcases clean, remove makeup before sleep, and resist picking. Hydration and barrier support matter even for oily skin.

title: Calming redness and barrier support
content: Redness often signals a stressed skin barrier. Prioritize fragrance-free moisturizer with ceramides, niacinamide for calming, and consistent broad-spectrum SPF. Pause strong exfoliants or retinoids if skin feels hot, stinging, or tight. Cool water rinses and gentle pat-drying help.

title: Common redness triggers
content: Sun exposure without SPF, harsh cleansers, over-exfoliation, spicy foods, alcohol, stress, and new actives without patch testing can increase visible redness. A minimal routine for one to two weeks can help identify triggers.

title: Morning skincare routine framework
content: A balanced morning routine: gentle cleanser or water rinse if skin is dry, antioxidant or hydrating serum optional, moisturizer matched to skin type, and SPF 30+ as the final step. Reapply SPF every two hours with prolonged outdoor exposure.

title: Night skincare routine framework
content: Evening routine: remove sunscreen and makeup with gentle cleanser, hydrating toner or essence, one targeted treatment (salicylic acid, retinol, or niacinamide — not all together initially), then moisturizer. Alternate treatment nights to reduce irritation.

title: Niacinamide guidance
content: Niacinamide (vitamin B3) supports oil balance, redness calming, and barrier function. It is generally well tolerated and pairs with most routines. Typical use is once or twice daily in serum or moisturizer form. Patch test if skin is very reactive.

title: Retinol introduction
content: Retinol supports cell turnover but can cause dryness and irritation when overused. Start one to two nights per week on dry skin after moisturizer (sandwich method). Do not combine with strong exfoliating acids on the same night. Always use SPF the following morning.

title: Vitamin C and antioxidants
content: Vitamin C serums can support brightness and antioxidant defense. Use in the morning under SPF. If irritation occurs, reduce frequency or choose a lower concentration. Store away from heat and light per product instructions.

title: Salicylic acid for pores and congestion
content: Salicylic acid (BHA) is oil-soluble and helps with pore congestion and mild breakouts. Use as cleanser or leave-on treatment two to three nights weekly at first. Avoid using with retinol or strong AHAs on the same night.

title: Combining actives safely
content: Do not stack retinol, salicylic acid, and glycolic acid on the same night. Niacinamide generally pairs well with most ingredients. When adding a new active, wait two to four weeks before introducing another. Patch test on the jawline first.

title: Hydration and moisture balance
content: Hydration comes from humectants (hyaluronic acid, glycerin) and is sealed with occlusive or emollient moisturizers. Even oily skin needs moisture. Dehydrated skin can produce more oil and feel tight simultaneously.

title: Pore visibility and care
content: Pore size is largely genetic; routines can reduce visibility through consistent cleansing, hydration, and occasional BHA use. Avoid pore strips and harsh squeezing. Niacinamide and retinol may improve appearance over time with patience.

title: Improving skin texture
content: Texture improves with consistent hydration, gentle exfoliation one to two times weekly, and steady SPF. Avoid changing products weekly. Retinol and AHAs can help but require slow introduction and barrier support.

title: Sun protection essentials
content: Daily broad-spectrum SPF 30+ is the most important anti-aging and redness-prevention step. Apply enough product (about a quarter teaspoon for face). Reapply with outdoor exposure. SPF is essential when using retinol or acids.

title: Skin type and routine matching
content: Oily skin: gel cleanser, lightweight moisturizer, non-comedogenic SPF. Dry skin: cream cleanser, richer moisturizer, hydrating serums. Combination skin: balance T-zone oil control with cheek hydration. Sensitive skin: minimal fragrance-free products and slow active introduction.

title: Educational boundaries
content: Skincare guidance is educational, not medical diagnosis. Persistent pain, bleeding lesions, rapidly changing moles, or severe cystic acne warrant professional evaluation. Skinova helps interpret trends and routine choices, not replace dermatology care.

title: Reading skin analysis scores
content: Analysis scores reflect visible patterns like texture, redness, pores, and breakout risk. Higher scores generally indicate healthier signals in that category. Focus on the top two to three concerns rather than chasing perfect numbers. Track trends across scans, not single snapshots.

title: Tracking improvement over time
content: Meaningful skin changes often take four to eight weeks of consistent routine. Photograph in similar lighting for comparison. Improve one variable at a time. Sleep, hydration, stress, and diet also influence visible skin.

title: Getting reliable scan photos
content: For best analysis: front-facing selfie, face centered filling most of the frame, even lighting, minimal blur, no heavy filters, JPG or PNG under 10MB. Avoid group photos, side profiles, or cropped faces.

title: What Skinova Skin Coach does
content: Skinova Skin Coach answers skincare education questions using your latest scan context and Skinova's curated knowledge base. It explains acne risk, pores, redness, texture, hydration, and oiliness scores from YouCam Skin Analysis. It generates routine guidance and ingredient cautions. It does not diagnose disease, prescribe medication, or recommend specific branded products.

title: Interpreting acne risk scores in Skinova
content: In Skinova, acne risk reflects visible breakout patterns and congestion — not a medical diagnosis. Lower scores suggest higher visible concern. When acne risk is elevated, Skinova recommends gentle cleansing, non-comedogenic moisturizer, SPF, and salicylic acid limited to two or three nights weekly. Avoid adding multiple actives at once. Track whether the score improves over four to eight weeks of a steady routine.

title: Interpreting redness scores in Skinova
content: Redness scores in Skinova reflect visible irritation and uneven tone signals. When redness is a top concern, prioritize barrier repair: fragrance-free moisturizer, niacinamide, and daily SPF. Pause strong exfoliants if skin feels hot or stinging. Redness can fluctuate with weather, stress, and new products — compare trends across scans rather than one snapshot.

title: Interpreting pore scores in Skinova
content: Pore visibility scores describe how prominent pores appear in the scan — largely influenced by oil, hydration, and lighting. Skinova suggests consistent cleansing, hydration, niacinamide, and occasional BHA rather than aggressive squeezing or pore strips. Improvement is gradual; focus on routine consistency.

title: Interpreting texture scores in Skinova
content: Texture scores reflect surface smoothness and evenness. When texture is a focus area, maintain hydration, gentle exfoliation one to two times weekly maximum, and steady SPF. Retinol may help over time but requires slow introduction. Avoid changing products weekly — texture responds to consistency.

title: Interpreting hydration scores in Skinova
content: Hydration scores estimate moisture balance in the visible skin surface. Low hydration can coexist with oily skin (dehydration). Skinova recommends humectants like hyaluronic acid or glycerin sealed with moisturizer morning and night. Even breakout-prone skin needs moisture to support the barrier.

title: Interpreting oiliness in Skinova scans
content: Oiliness signals help tune cleanser and moisturizer weight. Over-stripping oily skin can increase oil production. Use gel or low-foam cleansers, lightweight non-comedogenic moisturizer, and niacinamide. Avoid skipping moisturizer because skin feels oily.

title: How Skinova builds routines from scans
content: Skinova's Routine page derives morning and night steps from your top scan concerns. Morning emphasizes cleanse, optional niacinamide, moisturizer, and SPF. Night emphasizes cleanse, hydration, one targeted treatment on alternate nights, and barrier moisturizer. Caution notes flag ingredient conflicts (e.g., do not stack retinol and salicylic acid the same night).

title: Using niacinamide with salicylic acid
content: Niacinamide and salicylic acid can often be used in the same routine when skin tolerates it: niacinamide morning or both times for calming and oil balance; salicylic acid as a leave-on treatment two to three nights weekly. If irritation appears, separate them (BHA at night, niacinamide morning) or reduce BHA frequency. Patch test first.

title: Why skin may look redder this week
content: Short-term redness increases can come from new actives, over-exfoliation, sun exposure without SPF, harsh cleansers, stress, or lack of sleep. Skinova suggests a minimal routine for one to two weeks: gentle cleanser, ceramide moisturizer, niacinamide, and SPF. Pause retinol and acids until skin feels calm. Compare your redness score across scans after stabilizing the routine.

title: Reducing breakout risk without harsh products
content: Gentle approaches for breakout-prone skin: low-foam cleanser twice daily, lightweight non-comedogenic moisturizer, daily SPF, and salicylic acid two to three nights weekly — not every night. Avoid physical scrubs and picking. Introduce one new product every two to four weeks. Barrier support reduces irritation that can worsen visible breakouts.

title: What a Skinova-aligned morning routine includes
content: Skinova's default morning framework: gentle cleanse (or water rinse if very dry), niacinamide if redness or oiliness is a concern, moisturizer matched to skin type, and broad-spectrum SPF 30+ as the final step. Antioxidants like vitamin C are optional if tolerated. Keep the morning routine simple to maintain consistency.

title: Topics Skin Coach cannot answer
content: Skin Coach cannot provide medical diagnosis, prescription advice, emergency triage, legal or financial guidance, or unrelated general knowledge. It does not recommend specific prescription drugs or guarantee treatment outcomes. For persistent pain, bleeding lesions, or rapidly changing moles, seek professional care. Redirect questions to acne, redness, pores, texture, hydration, routines, ingredients, or scan interpretation.

title: How Skinova uses YouCam Skin Analysis
content: Skinova sends your selfie through YouCam Skin Analysis server-side (credentials never reach the browser). The API returns concern scores such as acne, pores, texture, redness, and moisture. Skinova maps those into plain-language insights, routine steps, and coach context. Scores are educational signals for consumer guidance — not clinical test results.

title: Fine lines and aging signals in scans
content: When wrinkle or aging signals appear in analysis, Skinova focuses on prevention: daily SPF, consistent moisturizer, and slow retinol introduction if appropriate for your barrier. Hydration and sun protection are foundational. Avoid aggressive treatments without professional guidance for deep medical concerns.

title: Coaching when no scan is available
content: Without a recent scan, Skin Coach provides general Skinova education on routines, ingredients, and concern categories. Answers are grounded in the knowledge base only — not personalized to your scores. Run a Skin Scan for concern-specific guidance tied to your acne risk, redness, pores, texture, and hydration signals.

title: Skinova progress and improvement story
content: The Progress page projects trend movement from your latest scan concerns. It is an educational story to encourage routine consistency — not a medical forecast or guaranteed visual outcome. Compare scans every four to eight weeks in similar lighting. Change one routine variable at a time to understand what helps.

title: Introducing actives on sensitive skin
content: For reactive skin: use fragrance-free basics for two weeks before any active. Patch test on the jawline for three nights. Introduce niacinamide before acids or retinol. Wait two to four weeks between new products. If stinging persists, simplify to cleanser, moisturizer, and SPF only until the barrier calms.
